messages:
anna: heads-up: opened MR that shifts the billing service SA and kms grant into infra/billing. moving from Helm-managed SA to tf-managed IRSA role + kms grant. would love quick sanity checks on ordering and rollback impact

derek: link? also which pattern are you using for the grant: aws_kms_grant or modifying key policy? those have slightly different eventual consistency semantics

anna: MR: https://gitlab.redwood/internal/infra/merge_requests/412 
changes: modules/billing/service_account.tf + kms/grants.tf + provider.kubernetes usage to create a small marker secret

vishal: short answer: both have races. aws_kms_grant is an API-level object attached to the key and will be visible quickly, but pods that mount secrets via secrets-store-csi can still start before the grant exists. key policy changes can be slower to propagate depending on caches.

jen: can you paste the tf grant snippet? curious whether grantee_principal is the role ARN or OIDC-subject (svc acct). we prefer role ARN for tf-managed role objects

anna: here's the simplified snippet:

```
resource "aws_iam_role" "billing_irsa" {
  name = "billing-svc-role"
  # trust relationship -> OIDC provider + condition for namespace/serviceaccount
}

resource "aws_kms_grant" "billing_decrypt" {
  key_id = aws_kms_key.billing.id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.billing_irsa.arn
  operations = ["Decrypt", "GenerateDataKey"]
}
```

anna: then I create a kubernetes_secret "billing-kms-ready" using the kubernetes provider with depends_on = [aws_kms_grant.billing_decrypt] so Helm can gate install on that secret existing

mark: sounds reasonable. couple of thoughts: 1) if Helm is run by CI (helmfile/argocd), the timing differs. argocd will pull chart and apply, it won't wait on an external k8s secret unless you add a pre-sync hook. 2) if the SA annotation is applied earlier by a separate process (helm chart creating svcacct annotations), the pod may start and fail until grant appears

vishal: to handle argocd, we did this pattern before: tf creates the grant + a small k8s ConfigMap marker in the target namespace. In the chart we add a pre-install hook that does a blocking check for that ConfigMap. For argocd, you can use resource hooks or a custom health check that waits for marker. Works well in practice

jen: alternative: create a conservative key policy that permits the OIDC provider or the entire account to Decrypt, and then a narrower grant created later for the role only. That way pods won't fail on first start while you converge to least-privilege. downside: key policy broadness and audit noise

anna: I wanted to avoid changing key policy since auditors like minimal key policy edits. the marker secret approach seemed least invasive

mark: minor improvement: add lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true } where appropriate and ensure role and grants are in same apply to reduce windows. but tf can't guarantee the order between k8s cluster applying annotations and pod kubelet starting.

vishal: another trick: use kubelet-level toleration by adding an initContainer that blocks until the ConfigMap/secret exists. easier than trying to control helm/argocd ordering. init container can loop and retry with exponential backoff for up to X minutes

anna: example init container snippet for chart values I added:

```yaml
initContainers:
- name: wait-for-kms-grant
  image: bitnami/kubectl:latest
  command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "for i in $(seq 1 30); do kubectl get configmap billing-kms-ready -n {{ .Release.Namespace }} && exit 0; sleep 5; done; exit 1"]
  resources: {}
```

jen: that approach is solid and keeps infra changes simpler. downside: adds extra start latency to pods until the grant is present

derek: also think about cleanup: if the grant is rotated or key re-created, stale marker may mislead. make marker creation include a timestamp and a simple sidecar/cronjob that reconciles marker existence vs grant existence and removes stale markers older than, say, 10 minutes

anna: good call. I'll add metadata and TTL label. plan: update MR to create k8s ConfigMap with label grant_ts = RFC3339 timestamp and the kubernetes_manifest will have depends_on the aws_kms_grant. also add a small cleanup job in infra that prunes markers older than 30m

mark: one more: CI tests. add a staging pipeline step that does terraform apply -> check for configmap -> helm upgrade --wait. that caught a flake we had where the grant failed due to missing kms:Encrypt in a dependent service

deploy-bot: Pipeline 5821: terraform plan succeeded for MR 412. apply scheduled on staging runner.

anna: thanks all. will push changes: configmap + initContainer example + cleanup job + PR note about rollback scenario (if tf rollback removes grant but chart already added annotation, the app should tolerate decrypt errors via retry/backoff). will ping when staging pipeline runs

vishal: lgtm. consider adding a short troubleshooting checklist to the PR template: how to detect grant vs policy issues, commands to list grants, and quick fix steps

anna: will add checklist. merging after staging green. appreciate the quick reviews.
